workflow_runs.display_title: redesign the settings panel after dsh-our-free-model (0.8.0)

head_commit.message:
redesign the settings panel after dsh-our-free-model (0.8.0)

The reference is a React standalone page; this is imperative DOM inside a DSH panel, so
the framework differs but the visual language transfers.

Setting rows were label / control / value on one line, which gave three things the same
narrow column and left no room for an explanation, so every explanation piled up at the
bottom of the card. All 14 rows now read as one item per line: title in 13px dark text,
a grey sub-line under it, control on the right. Slider rows use a wide variant with the
control on its own line. A hairline separates the items, so each setting explains itself.

All 15 cards are now boxed (white, 12px radius, hairline border) and 14 gained a group
description. This reverses an earlier decision recorded in the dsw-card comment, which
argued against identical outlined boxes and preferred section headings with negative
space. The reversal is deliberate since the user asked for the reference styling, but the
side effect is more visual weight, most visible at the 560px panel width. Dropping boxed
from the data-heavy cards would restore the lighter look.

Two parts of the reference were not copied: the left sidebar navigation, because the
panel is about 560px wide and a sidebar would squeeze the content, and the bottom
undo / save bar, because settings here take effect immediately and there is nothing to
undo.

One trap worth recording: styles live inside a template literal, and I put a backtick
around a class name in a CSS comment. That ended the template early and tsc reported
TS1005. Class names in those comments must not be wrapped in backticks.

Moving the description out of the switch label left four checkboxes and five range
inputs without an accessible name, so aria-label was added to each.

tsc, build, bundle, isolation and 68/68 files pass. Light and dark previews checked
screen by screen; the preview fixture now matches the new structure.

workflow_runs.name: Release
workflow_runs.display_title: fix: quitting DSH erased the persistence it had just written (0.7.5)

head_commit.message:
fix: quitting DSH erased the persistence it had just written (0.7.5)

disposeSessionReuse() is the unload hook (index.ts ctx.effect(() => () => ...)). It
cleared the in memory slots and chains and then called persistResumeState(), writing
the empty state back to resume-state.json. So every quit wiped the file, and
restoreResumeState() read back nothing on the next start. The 0.6.43 fix, shipping in
0.6.43 and still advertised through 0.7.4, never took effect in real use.

Symptom: the same conversation line was forced onto a fresh web session, which shows
up as a Modify / Regenerate fork. Measured at 270k characters of full resend.

persistResumeState now takes an optional persist flag and the three clearing
functions pass false: disposeSessionReuse, resetSessionReuse and resetContextChain.
The other eight call sites are real adds, updates and deletes, so they still persist.

It was green the whole time because check-resume-after-restart only covers process to
process and never goes through the unload hook, while check-bundle only asserted that
a persist call exists, not what it wrote. Adding persistence means testing the exit to
startup boundary; that is now covered by tests/check-persist-lifecycle.mjs, which
seeds a non empty file through writeResumeStateForTest and asserts the three clearing
functions leave the contents alone. Reverting all three to persistResumeState() turns
all three assertions red.

The new check-bundle guard for the unload hook call site was itself always true: the
slice contains a comment line mentioning disposeSessionReuse(), so deleting the real
call still matched. It now compares whole lines instead. That is another case of an
assertion being satisfied by a comment, same root cause as the existing rule 3.

tsc, build, bundle, the three new guards, the external review guards,
check-resume-after-restart, isolation and 68/68 files pass.
